## What's new

### Flock support: every app and every agent at its own .test URL
Larvyn now works with [Flock](https://flockphp.com), the free local PHP environment for Windows, macOS and Linux. It's optional: nothing changes until Flock is installed. Then the Overview gets a **Local site** card:
- **Serve** an app at `<folder>.test` in one click. `APP_URL` follows when it was still `localhost`, with a backup of `.env`, and goes back when you **Stop serving**.
- An **HTTPS** switch with a certificate your browsers already trust, and a **PHP version** picker per app. A version Flock doesn't have yet downloads with its progress shown in the card.
- **Every agent's worktree is served at its own URL** (`larvyn-<task>.<app>.test`) and set up by Flock. A 🌐 button on each agent opens its attempt in the browser, so you can compare the results before you merge.
- The dev stack hands the HTTP server over to Flock. Vite, the queue and the rest still start from Larvyn.
- Laravel apps you add to Larvyn are served right away (**Settings → Flock** turns this off). If Flock isn't set up or isn't running, the card offers **Set up** or **Start**.

[Read more on the blog](https://larvyn.dev/blog/flock-integration/).

### A first-run setup
New installs open a short setup in three steps:
- It checks your toolchain: PHP, Node and Git, plus Composer, the Laravel installer and a local server (Flock or Herd).
- It picks your editor, your default agent and whether agents ask before acting.
- It ends on your first app.

**Settings → Run the setup again** brings it back.

## Fixes
- **OpenCode lost its first prompt** when it started in a fresh worktree, which is always the case when one task goes to several agents. The prompt is now passed on the command line. ([#3](https://github.com/larvyn/releases/issues/3))
- **Restored terminals typed stray characters** such as `1;2c` or `^[[I` at the prompt, because replaying the saved output made the terminal answer old queries. Both are gone.

## Under the hood
- The last services moved into `internal/` packages (laravel, project, system, composer), and `main.go` now only wires the app.
- CI fails when Go files aren't `gofmt`'d.
